newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB may ship more grain on Mississippi barges.
newsitem.headline: CWB may ship more grain on Mississippi barges.

text.p: Canadian wheat may be shipped to Central America in the future on barges navigating the Mississippi River after a successful maiden voyage in July, a Canadian Wheat Board spokesman said.

"Yes, depending on the logistics and the costs. The exchange rate's a big factor and it becomes competitive when you're south of Minneapolis when you start getting barge competition with rail, but up to Minneapolis it's pretty high rates," CWB spokesman Jim Pietryk said.
About 3,000 tonnes of durum wheat were shipped to Panama and Costa Rica in July on Mississippi barges, Pietryk said.
"We did it just to see how it works. I know we've gone out of the (U.S.) Pacific Northwest on a trial basis before," he added.

The durum was loaded on rail cars in Moose Jaw and Rosetown, Saskatchewan, and railed to St. barges which transferred the grain to export terminals in Remy, Louisiana, CWB Latin America and Caribbean senior marketing manager Rhyl Doyle said.
Panama and Costa Rica are difficult countries to service from Canada because they are small markets and often delivery is not economical, Doyle said.
